    - Jory! Quay porter, like my ma before me. She carried cargo here thirty years, till her back gave out. I took over at fourteen.
    - When I'm not hauling, I'm in Tamsin's yard. She works me harder than any captain. Once she said I was the best thing to happen to the boat in years. By accident. I pretended not to hear, so she can't take it back.
    - Want to hear Ma's last letter? 'Dear Jory, the hens are well, your aunt is well, I am mostly well. Do not row too hard.'
    - She always says do not row too hard. I read it out to the whole quay, and now the whole quay says it to me. Do not row too hard, Jory. I row too hard.
